grain.note: A 6% black line of the wood grain, over the wood gradient; not a solid color.

display.purpose: The result title, "Victory" or "Defeat". 1.5rem on a short screen.

headline.purpose: Screen titles such as the Campaign header, with a hard 3px drop shadow. The Turn banner uses Cinzel 900 at 1.5rem.

title.purpose: Panel labels, the Tutorial step title, Stage and Deck names, the Start Battle label, the Key Guide title, and the Building labels in the Town (at least 14px, scaled with the painting).

body.purpose: The Details Panel, the Tutorial text, the dialog text. Keywords are Inter 700 in keyword-rust.

body-small.purpose: Reminder text, Deck descriptions, the Key Guide list. Flavor text is the same size in italic.

label.purpose: Small uppercase section labels such as "Tutorial". Town Bar shortcut names use Inter 700 at 11px (10px under 1200px), not uppercase.

number.purpose: Countdowns, Attack, HP, pile counts and the Turn number, in tabular figures. On a card, 1.2em to 1.3em of the card font size, with a small dark text shadow.

micro.purpose: The number on a small count token, and the compact labels of a short screen. It is the one size below Label.

shadows.name: piece-drop
shadows.purpose: Every button and HUD tooltip. A Town Bar icon has the same drop at 2px, as drop-shadow. Pressed: 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.45) and the piece moves down 1px.

shadows.name: card-bevel
shadows.purpose: The Card Frame and the Card Back.

shadows.name: well
shadows.purpose: An empty Hand Slot or an empty pile.

shadows.name: badge-drop
shadows.purpose: Round card badges and stat plates.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The Card Details over the Board (a filter).

shadows.name: panel-drop
shadows.purpose: The soft drop of the Stage Panel and other parchment sheets that float over a screen.

shadows.name: active-glow
shadows.purpose: The Hero panel (or Boss plate) of the side whose Turn it is.

shadows.name: selected-halo
shadows.purpose: A selected option card, a selected Battle Log entry.

shadows.name: building-glow
shadows.purpose: A Town Building under the pointer or the focus, and an Open or Done Stage Marker under the pointer, in focus or selected (a filter).

shadows.name: tutorial-glow
shadows.purpose: The part of the screen that a Tutorial step points to, with a 4px tutorial-glow ring.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The focus ring on every interactive piece, and the ring on a selected Hand Card.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button hover brightness and the 1px press.

motion.name: ease-deal
motion.purpose: The shared ease: the hand draw, the graveyard drop, Hints, panel ink-in and card deals.

motion.name: ease-lift
motion.purpose: Things that lift or slide into place: the Pack fan, the selected Pack on the Handbook shelf, the Handbook in the Battle.

motion.name: banner-in
motion.purpose: Banners and dialogs fade and zoom in from 95%.

motion.name: hint-pop
motion.purpose: A Hint grows out of the tip of its pointer, lifts away and settles from 102%.

motion.name: hint-seal
motion.purpose: The Hint seal stamps onto the parchment from 150%, turned 14°.

motion.name: hint-time
motion.purpose: The Hint time line gets shorter until the Hint closes; it stops while the pointer or focus holds the Hint.

motion.name: settings-sheet
motion.purpose: The Settings dialog, the Stage Panel and the Floor Panel come up out of their button, marker or Floor stone on a curved path.

motion.name: stage-panel-ink
motion.purpose: Panel parts ink in from the top: rise 6px and fade in. The docked Dungeon Panel inks in a new Dungeon, and the light of a Boss on the painting inks in (200ms).

motion.name: stage-panel-deal
motion.purpose: A reward card is dealt onto the page from 120% and 12°, and lands at its own tilt.

motion.name: pack-stamp
motion.purpose: A stamp lands: the NEW chip, the Max seal, the "Bounty claimed" stamp, the Sweep ×N stamp, the check of a won Floor stone.

motion.name: mine-wake
motion.value: the world 380ms cubic-bezier(0.33, 0.9, 0.28, 1) +220ms per further stop; the light of a stop 900ms ease-out at +300ms; the lift cage 420ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)
motion.purpose: The Dungeons mine: the world slides to the new stop and the lift stays, so a deeper ride takes more time; the light of a newly opened stop comes up one time (mine-wake); the lift cage rides the rope of the Depth Gauge to the selected stop.

motion.name: pack-open
motion.value: shake 520ms, tear 480-520ms, burst 800ms, fan 560ms +90ms per card
motion.purpose: A Pack lifts and shakes, tears on a zigzag, lets out a light in the color of its best card, and fans its Card Backs.

motion.name: pack-flip
motion.purpose: A Card Back turns on its vertical axis; the Rank light grows behind the face 200ms in.

motion.name: shop-lamp
motion.purpose: The lamps of the Card shop and the Workshop breathe.

motion.name: shop-sheen
motion.purpose: A line of light goes across a Pack or a Ready Gear item, masked by its image.

motion.name: workshop-flip
motion.purpose: A Combine or Craft turns the card over to the new copy.

motion.name: gear-strike
motion.purpose: A Gear upgrade: the Forge Stone leaps into the item, the item gives, sparks fly in the tier color, the plate glows once.

motion.name: handbook-side
motion.purpose: In the Battle, the Handbook slides in from the right and its cover swings open edge-on, never over the Board.

motion.name: log-panel
motion.purpose: The Battle Log unrolls from its top edge (a clip-path).

motion.name: keyword-plate
motion.purpose: A Keyword Plate grows over its Unit, rises a little and fades in its last 25%.

motion.name: boss-beats
motion.purpose: Dungeon beats: a Boss tips back and fades, a Front Bracket grows over new Lanes, a Boss Rule notch breaks and its label comes out.

motion.name: town-leave
motion.purpose: Zoom 12% toward a selected Building, then fade.

motion.name: screen-in
motion.purpose: The Campaign, Hero, Dungeons and Heynspire screens fade in.

motion.name: campaign-marker-in
motion.purpose: Stage Markers rise onto their clearings in Trail order: down 14px from 86% size, with a fade.

motion.name: campaign-trail-draw
motion.purpose: The walked part of the Trail draws in from the Trail entry.

motion.name: campaign-open-pulse
motion.purpose: The Open Stage Marker and the Current Floor stone: the ready-gold halo pulses (town-gate-pulse) and a gold-light ground ring ripples out (campaign-ripple).

motion.name: campaign-awaken
motion.purpose: One time, a Stage that a win just opened, or the new Current Floor stone, wakes up: grey 70% to bright 116%, then settles, with an expanding focus-cream ring.

motion.name: flight-fold
motion.purpose: A Flight of the Floor rail folds to its band and unfolds to its stair (grid rows 0fr to 1fr), as the pool plate of the Packs screen.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All animation, ambient motion and the camera stop when the Player asks for reduced motion; things show at once.

breakpoints.name: short-screen
breakpoints.purpose: The phone-in-landscape layout. Every component has a compact form.

breakpoints.name: tall-screen
breakpoints.purpose: Room for stacked plates, such as Cards found under the pool plate on the Packs screen.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: The Battle Log becomes a sheet over the bottom of the Board.

breakpoints.name: compact-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Boss plates drop their names; Pack pool names go to screen readers only; the shopkeeper is quiet.

breakpoints.name: town-bar-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Town Bar names drop to 10px and the Settings slot narrows.

breakpoints.name: portrait-guard
breakpoints.purpose: A phone in portrait shows only a request to turn the phone.

components.name: Gold Button
components.description: The one main action of a panel, such as End Turn or Start Battle.

components.name: Wood Button
components.description: The default button, for the second action of a panel.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Small HUD controls over the Board: speed, Skip, sound, Key Guide.

components.name: Turn Badge
components.description: A Night Plate HUD piece with the Turn number and the Your Turn chip.

components.description: A radio choice on parchment, such as a Stage or a Starter Deck.

components.description: A result or confirm dialog: parchment, a thick frame-wood border, one gold and one wood action.

components.name: Mine Stop
components.description: Dungeons signature: one stop of the mine, the painted lair of one Dungeon. The same lift cut-out stands in the empty lift well at its left, on the floor line, and the shaft rock fills what is left of the screen. The Depth Gauge at the left selects the stop: a rope with one marker for each Dungeon and the iron lift cage around the selected one. The docked Dungeon Panel at the right carries one Boss Dossier for each Boss. Hover or focus on a dossier lights that Boss on the painting (a warm glow in screen blend); after a win, the claimed stamp lands at the feet of each Boss. The world slides on a ride and the lift stays.

narrative.overview:
Heynbord is a painted fantasy card game. The Battle is a painted battlefield (web ADR-0006), the Units are figures on it, and every 2D control is a real game piece at the edge of that painting: a wooden tray for the Hand, bronze frames for the cards, a leather Card Back, gold tokens for the actions, and parchment sheets for the rules. The world is bright, warm, clear, handmade and a little funny, like a classic adventure story. The UI never tries to be a web app around a game. It is part of the game box.

The material is a frame, not a surface for text. Wood, bronze and leather carry gradients, bevels and grain, but all text sits on a flat area with high contrast: cream on a dark plate, or dark ink on parchment. Pieces are chunky and tactile. They have thick borders, a hard drop under each button, and a small physical press. The density is that of a board game: a few large pieces, each easy to read on a phone in landscape.

The system is light and readable first (product pillar 5). The HUD sits at the edges of the screen and lets pointer events through to the Board. Effects and panels never hide the Board or the stats. Motion is short and physical, and reduced motion stops all of it.

There is one theme. The base component library in `apps/web/src/core/styles/globals.css` reads semantic names (`bg`, `fg`, `primary`, `danger`), and every one of those names is an alias of a Heynbord material token. The Component Catalog, the landing page and the game screens resolve to the same palette. The game world that this file describes is normative.
keyCharacteristics: Real materials as frames: dark wood, warm bronze, gold, tooled leather, parchment.
Text on flat, high-contrast areas only: cream on a night plate, or ink on parchment.
Chunky pieces: 2px to 4px borders, a hard 3px drop with no blur, a 1px press.
Gold means "act now" or "this is yours": the main action, a Ready card, Your Turn, the current screen.
Game meaning is never shown by color alone: Rank uses gems and a count, Damage Type uses a color and an icon.
One gold focus ring (`focus-cream`, 4px) on every interactive piece.
A compact layout for short screens (`max-height: 500px`) on every component.

rules.name: The Gold Means Act Rule
rules.body: Gold marks the main action of a panel, a Ready card, Your Turn, and the current place. Each panel has one gold action. Wood is the default for all other buttons.

rules.name: The Flat Text Rule
rules.body: Text never sits on a gradient, a grain or the 3D scene. It sits on a flat Night Plate, on parchment, or on a solid button face, with WCAG 2.2 AA contrast.

rules.name: The Never Color Alone Rule
rules.body: A Rank always has its gems (1 for Common to 5 for Legendary). A Damage Type always has its icon. A side always has its position (player left, enemy right) as well as its color.

rules.name: The Alias Contrast Rule
rules.body: A bright material does not always carry white text. `danger` uses `enemy-deep` with `cream` (11.16:1), not `enemy-red` with white (4.23:1). `success` uses `hp-full` with `ink-on-gold` (9.65:1). A new alias takes the darker or the lighter material that passes WCAG 2.2 AA.

rules.name: The One Theme Rule
rules.body: The application has one theme: the Heynbord material palette. There is no light mode and no dark mode. `core/components/ui` reads the semantic aliases, and every alias points at a material token. A second palette does not exist.

rules.name: The Large Display Rule
rules.body: Cinzel is for titles and names at 14px or larger. Never use it for rules text, Keywords, numbers or paragraphs.

rules.name: The Big Number Rule
rules.body: A number that the Player plans with (a Countdown, Attack, HP) is Inter 900 with tabular figures, on its own badge or plate. It is the largest text on its piece.

rules.name: The Short Screen Rule
rules.body: `@media (max-height: 500px)` is the phone-in-landscape layout. Every component has a compact form for it: smaller padding, one size smaller text, and icon-only Town Bar shortcuts. A phone in portrait shows only a request to turn the phone.

rules.name: The Clear Board Rule
rules.body: No HUD piece, panel or effect may cover a Square or a Unit stat for longer than an action needs. Card Details open at the sides of the Board, not on it. The Tutorial panel opens next to the thing that its step tells about, with a pointer to it: above the Hand, under the Summon Zone, under the Player's Units, or above or under the Lane to block. It never covers the Squares that its step points to. When there is no space next to the Lane to block, the panel opens at the right of the screen.

rules.name: The Markers In View Rule
rules.body: On every screen shape, from 4:3 to 21:9 and on a phone in landscape, all Stage Markers stay on the screen, above the Town Bar, and at least half of the Boss landmark stays in view. No Stage Marker goes under a HUD piece. The painting gets smaller before a marker goes off the screen or under the HUD.

rules.name: The Hard Drop Rule
rules.body: A piece that the Player can press casts a hard drop with no blur, and pressing it moves it down 1px. Soft, blurred shadows are only for things that float over the Board.

rules.name: The Glow Is State Rule
rules.body: A gold glow means Ready, active or selected. Never add a glow to a piece only to decorate it.

dos: Do put all text on a flat area: `cream` on a `night-plate`, or `ink` on `parchment`, at WCAG 2.2 AA contrast.
Do give each panel one gold action. Use wood for the second action and ghost for small controls over the Board.
Do give every interactive piece the 4px `focus-cream` ring, the Piece Drop and the 1px press.
Do show a Rank with its gems and a Damage Type with its icon, every time.
Do size card parts in `em`, and set the card size with the font size of the parent.
Do give every new component a compact form for `@media (max-height: 500px)`, and respect the safe-area insets.
Do stop all motion when the Player asks for reduced motion.
Do keep the art bright, warm and lit from the upper left, as art direction 5 asks.
donts: Don't make the game dark, realistic, gory, noisy or neon.
Don't use the blue primary, the zinc greys or the light/dark switch of the base component theme on a game screen.
Don't put text directly on wood grain, a bronze gradient, or a painting. On the Board, damage numbers and the Unit line use a dark outline.
Don't use Cinzel for rules text, Keywords, numbers, or any text under 14px.
Don't show a Rank, a Damage Type or a side by color alone.
Don't add a glow to a piece that is not Ready, active or selected.
Don't use soft, blurred shadows on buttons. They have a hard drop.
Don't cover a Square or a Unit stat with a HUD piece, a panel or an effect.
Don't use the Tutorial teal for anything except the Tutorial.
